rows.funding_note: Equity raised totals at least US$97 million, a floor because the seed and Series B amounts were never published. Series A: US$12 million, announced 14 Sep 2015, led by Vertex Ventures and Sinar Mas Digital Ventures with Asia Venture Group, BEENEXT, Ardent Capital, 500 Startups and Cherry Ventures (HappyFresh's own release; TechCrunch, 16 Sep 2015). Series B: led by Samena Capital with Vertex Ventures and Sinar Mas Digital Ventures, announced 29 Aug 2016 without an amount (TechCrunch), so it is not counted; the US$12 million that TechCrunch later cited is the Series A alone, so no round is counted twice. Series C: US$20 million, announced in April 2019, led by the Mirae Asset-Naver Asia Growth Fund with Line Ventures, Singha Ventures and Grab Ventures (TechCrunch, 22 Apr 2019; The Nation, 24 Apr 2019; HappyFresh's own blog). Series D: US$65 million, announced 27 Jul 2021, led by Naver Financial and Gafina B.V. with STIC Investments, LB Investment and Mirae Asset, and returning investors Mirae Asset-Naver Asia Growth Fund and Z Venture Capital (TechCrunch, 27 Jul 2021; HappyFresh's own release, 28 Jul 2021; The Jakarta Post). Bloomberg, carried by The Business Times on 7 Sep 2022, put the total at 'at least US$97 million in equity funding in addition to debt financing'. Not counted: the money that let HappyFresh resume in Indonesia in September 2022, which was venture debt from Genesis, InnoVen and Mars (Kumparan and Katadata, 22-23 Sep 2022). Why the group figure is kept: the rounds were raised by the Singapore holding company, iCart Group Pte. Ltd. (Rajah & Tann's Series D deal note), but the group was headquartered and run from Jakarta from the start (HappyFresh's own 2015 release; Jakarta Globe, 14 Sep 2015; Bloomberg, 2022, which calls Indonesia its home market), and its Malaysian, Thai and earlier Taiwanese and Philippine businesses were arms of that Jakarta-run company; today it operates only in Indonesia. So it is counted as an Indonesian company with a Singapore holding company, not as a foreign group's Indonesian arm. That holding company has since been wound up: a provisional liquidator was appointed on 18 Jul 2023 after its director declared that it could not continue by reason of its liabilities, and on 17 Aug 2023 it resolved to wind up voluntarily (Singapore Government Gazette, 21 Jul and 23 Aug 2023; DealStreetAsia, 20 Jul 2023), with the final meeting called for 26 Sep 2025. The investors' money went into that company; the Indonesian operating company, PT iCart Group Indonesia, kept trading, and who owns it now is not public. In May-September 2026 DealStreetAsia reported that Sayurbox and HappyFresh were weighing a merger, the second report noting a link to Trikomsel; no deal has been announced.

closed_add.name: RAENA
closed_add.sector: Commerce — beauty social-commerce app: resellers and dropshippers in Indonesia sold skincare, make-up and body-care products from partner brands, which Raena stocked and shipped for them
closed_add.why: RAENA ran a beauty social-commerce app for Indonesia: resellers and dropshippers picked skincare, make-up and body-care products from partner brands in the app and sold them on social media and online marketplaces, while Raena handled stock, supplier management and shipping, so sellers needed no inventory of their own. It was founded in Singapore in 2019 by Sreejita Deb (CEO) and Guo Xing Lim (COO), started out making beauty brands with social-media influencers, and moved to the reseller model in 2020; it operated in Indonesia through PT Raena Ruma Indonesia, registered in South Jakarta. Raena announced on Instagram that it was ending operations and that its app could no longer be used, saying it had worked with more than 45,000 entrepreneurs and 600 brands since 2019 (Uzone.id, 10 Feb 2025); DealStreetAsia reported the shutdown on 7 Feb 2025. In September 2025 the company's LinkedIn page wrote that earlier that year, 'in the face of unprecedented macro economic conditions', it had made the decision to bring Raena's operations to a close. Its reseller app is no longer on Google Play, and its old domain raenabeauty.com now carries an unrelated online-gambling page (both checked 17 Oct 2026). The funding figure is the total of about US$21 million reported by Hybrid.co.id in January 2022, made up of a US$1.82 million seed round announced in July 2019, a US$9 million Series A in February 2021 co-led by Alpha Wave Incubation and Alpha JWC Ventures with AC Ventures and the earlier investors Beenext, Beenos and Strive, and a US$10 million Series A extension in January 2022 led by Alpha Wave Incubation and AC Ventures with Alfamart and Alto Partners; no later round is on record. Sources differ on the founding year (AC Ventures gave 2018, some later reports 2020); 2019 follows Raena's own farewell message and TechCrunch.
